recommendation.bottom_line: Make the highest-EV free transfer (Martinez → Tzolakis, net +4.17) and captain Bruno Fernandes vs a leaky Everton — he is the only captain option with confirmed form, starts confirmed, and a soft opponent today.

transfer.rationale: Martinez is a structural liability: he has pulled out of matches in warm-ups on multiple occasions this season with a recurring calf issue and has since moved clubs (to Chelsea), making his FPL availability deeply unreliable. Tzolakis is the single highest net-gain transfer on the board (+4.17 projected points, no hit cost). He kept a clean sheet and made key saves vs Man United in GW1 and has 26 FPL points already at just £4.6m. Hull face a tough schedule (FDR avg 4.33 GW4-9) but that means saves volume — exactly what a budget keeper needs to score. This is the clearest, highest-confidence use of the free transfer.

chip.rationale: No chip clears the threshold this week across any profile. The 139-point deficit to the rival is large but still closeable across 34 remaining gameweeks — burning a chip in GW4 with no double gameweek or blanket advantage is negative expected value. Preserve chips for a confirmed DGW or Wildcard reset when squad value has grown.

captain.rationale: Fernandes is confirmed starting vs Everton today (Man Utd XI confirmed). He has 3 goals and 1 assist in just 180 PL minutes this season (FotMob avg rating 8.63) and scored a hat-trick + assist vs Ipswich in GW2 for 23 FPL points. Everton have conceded more big chances than any other team in the opening two gameweeks — the soft opponent upgrades his already elite form. De Cuyper has the highest projected EV (1.14) but that is a model projection for a £4.5m defender; Fernandes has the proven ceiling and confirmed start. João Pedro faces Arsenal away in GW3/4 — too tough for the armband.
